literal: Ear to-be-bitter words bearing quality possessing king's umbrella under will-stay world.
translation: The world will abide beneath the umbrella of a king who has the character to endure words that are bitter to the ear.
modern: தன் செவிக்குக் கசப்பாக இருக்கும் அறிவுரைகளையும் பொறுத்துக்கொள்ளும் பண்புடைய அரசனின் குடையின் கீழ்தான் உலகம் தங்கியிருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet describes the essential quality of a great ruler: the willingness to listen to harsh but necessary advice. The phrase 'cevi kaippa' literally means 'to be bitter to the ear', referring to words of criticism or correction. A king who possesses the character ('paṇpu') to bear ('poṟukkum') such words provides true protection. Consequently, the whole world ('ulaku') will willingly stay ('taṅkum') under his royal umbrella ('kavikai'), which serves as a traditional symbol of sovereign shelter and justice.
